title: Checked In
logline: a mockumentary about the overnight crew of a barely-haunted budget motel where the ghost is more of a roommate than a menace

style_guide.visual: desaturated indie mockumentary aesthetic with fluorescent overhead lighting, muted teals and yellows, grainy handheld documentary camera work with occasional static glitches during ghost appearances
style_guide.visual_negative: polished, glamorous, supernatural horror, dark shadows, vibrant colors, cinematic lighting
style_guide.writing: deadpan talking-heads interspersed with mundane workplace absurdism; comedy derives from characters treating the supernatural as bureaucratic inconvenience; awkward pauses and uncomfortable eye contact with camera; underreaction is the rule

sound_kit.score_mood: sparse indie folk with lonely electric guitar, muzak versions of public domain songs, the hum of ice machines
sound_kit.intro_jingle: 8 seconds of warped elevator music that briefly distorts with static before a tired ding of a front desk bell, ending on a sustained synth drone

appearance.canonical_descriptor: Marina Voss, 32, average build, shoulder-length straight black hair with blunt bangs, round tortoiseshell glasses, tired eyes with dark circles, wearing a wrinkled maroon polo shirt with name tag and khaki slacks, black non-slip shoes

personality.wants: to make it through her shift without incident and maybe feel less invisible
personality.comedic_function: straight-woman anchor who treats impossible situations as minor scheduling problems

speech.voice_hint: female, early 30s, flat midwestern affect, measured pace, slightly nasal, monotone

appearance.canonical_descriptor: Doug Pemberton, 28, lanky build, messy ginger hair sticking up in all directions, patchy beard, eager expression, wearing an oversized blue windbreaker over orange graphic tee with cartoon frog, baggy jeans with wallet chain, red high-top sneakers

personality.wants: to document proof of the paranormal and be taken seriously for once
personality.comedic_function: overreacts to everything, misreads situations, accidentally makes things worse while trying to help

speech.voice_hint: male, late 20s, excitable high register, rapid-fire pace, slight lisp, breathless

appearance.canonical_descriptor: Phyllis, appears 60s, translucent and slightly flickering, short curly gray hair, cat-eye glasses on chain, wearing a powder blue 1970s pantsuit with wide collar, pearl clip-on earrings, sensible cream loafers, holding a spectral clipboard

personality.wants: respect for the motel rules she wrote in 1978 and acknowledgment of her organizational contributions
personality.comedic_function: mundane ghost who complains about noise levels and thermostat settings rather than seeking vengeance

speech.voice_hint: female, mature, clipped precise diction, slow deliberate pace, tight-lipped disapproval, slight midwestern accent

locations.name: Front Desk
locations.canonical_descriptor: cramped front desk area with scuffed laminate counter, ancient beige computer monitor, rack of faded tourist brochures, water-stained acoustic ceiling tiles, flickering fluorescent lights, worn industrial carpet in burgundy and gold pattern, wall-mounted bell, plastic plant in corner

locations.name: Break Room
locations.canonical_descriptor: windowless break room with small round table, mismatched plastic chairs, humming mini-fridge covered in passive-aggressive notes, ancient microwave, cork board with OSHA posters and decade-old safety memos, yellowed walls, buzzing fluorescent strip light, coffee maker with permanent stains

season_arc.destination: The crew reluctantly admits they've become found family; Phyllis finally feels seen when they throw her a 45th death-iversary party; Marina accepts the night manager promotion she's been avoiding
season_arc.current_beat: Episode 1: A documentary crew arrives to film the 'haunted' Slumber Valley Inn; Marina insists there's nothing interesting to document while Phyllis floats through frame complaining about the camera crew not having a permit

canon_digest: Pilot. Nothing established yet beyond the bible.
